findings.where: tools/inbox.sh:39-44 (dbd3bed2); shown via tools/tick.sh:52 and hidden by tools/tick.sh:68
findings.problem: Off main, inbox.sh reads ONLY ssh/main's committed INBOX.md (MAIN_INBOX / inbox_text) and never looks at the working-tree INBOX.md. That working-tree file is where the logging chat on the same machine appends his words, uncommitted (the Mac's tree right now shows ` M INBOX.md`). So on the WSL laptop (branch port/wsl), or on a Mac checkout switched to a work branch, tick.sh's INBOX section says "inbox empty — INBOX.md on ssh/main and iCloud" while his unlogged notes are in the tree. next.sh:49-53 still reads the working tree and refuses to hand out work, but tick.sh:68 pipes next.sh through `sed -n '/^ACTIONABLE/,$p'`, which drops the STOP banner. The result is that tick shows 'inbox empty' and an empty queue. inbox.sh --done also refuses off main, so the tool can never drain notes that exist only on WSL, and next.sh blocks until someone edits the file by hand. Separately, next.sh:53 still writes .inbox-seen on any branch, which is the stale-snapshot case inbox.sh's own comment (lines 18-21) says it avoids. This is the failure the inbox header forbids: 'inbox empty' while his note sits unread. On the Mac it is a change of behaviour, because before this commit it read the working tree on every branch.
findings.fix: Off main, show the union of the two copies: the working tree's body below '---' plus ssh/main's body (de-duplicated). Label each part by where it came from, and keep a working-tree-only line out of 'inbox empty'. If a local line exists that ssh/main lacks, print a ⛔ banner last, so tick's tail shows it. Also make next.sh skip writing .inbox-seen when not on main, or have inbox.sh --done refuse a snapshot older than its own last display.
findings.evidence: inbox.sh:39 `MAIN_INBOX="$(git show ssh/main:INBOX.md)"`; :43 `inbox_text() { if [ "$ON_MAIN" = 1 ]; then cat INBOX.md; else printf '%s\n' "$MAIN_INBOX"; fi; }`; :112 prints 'inbox empty — $INBOX_NAME and iCloud…'. next.sh:49 `INBOX_BODY="$(sed -n '/^---$/,$p' INBOX.md …)"` (working tree). tick.sh:68 `./tools/next.sh 2>&1 | sed -n '/^ACTIONABLE/,$p'` filters out next.sh's STOP output.

findings.problem: If the CONTROL run returns NOSUITE, spotcheck exits 2 with 'the runner, Chrome or the server, not $SHORT. No verdict, nothing logged.' It does this without calling env_ok, the check it applies to the reverted side four lines later. NOSUITE covers _cdp.py's own timeout ('suite did not finish within 300s', exit 2, no summary), so a release whose changed test hangs or now takes more than 300 s is blamed on the machine. Its defect is never logged: before this commit it was logged as `NOT-PROVEN NO-CONTROL`, which tick.sh lists as an open defect. Every later spotcheck of that release repeats the same misdiagnosis. This changes Mac behaviour.
findings.fix: Treat a control NOSUITE the way the reverted side is treated: `env_ok || exit 2` (the machine's fault, no verdict). Otherwise tag it NO-CONTROL and log it, at least when the error is a timeout or a missing summary with Chrome and the server confirmed healthy.
findings.evidence: spotcheck.sh:117 `if [ "${r%%|*}" = NOSUITE ]; then echo "spotcheck: the control did not run … not $SHORT …"; exit 2`. Compare :143-144 `PASS/NOSUITE) env_ok || { …; exit 2; }; tag="NORUN"`. run_one :91-94 maps any output without a summary (timeout included) to NOSUITE. _cdp.py:544-548 prints the timeout error with no summary and returns 2.

findings.problem: The double-quote-title gate's regex is now stricter on the Mac too: `[^'\n]` became `[^']`. It is also not anchored to a test declaration, so it matches `test('` inside `.test('…`, `latest('`, `contest('` and similar. Any existing tests.js line such as `/re/.test('<b class="x">')` would now make EVERY Mac ship refuse in one second, saying 'a test title contains a double quote'. Whether such a line exists was not verified here, because the brief said not to grep tests.js.
findings.fix: Anchor it the way the vanished-test gate does: `grep -nE "^[[:space:]]*test\('[^']*\"[^']*'" tests/tests.js`. Before merging, confirm `git show dbd3bed2:tests/tests.js | grep -cE "test\('[^']*\"[^']*'"` prints 0 on the Mac.
findings.evidence: ship.sh:255 `_DQ="$(grep -nE "test\('[^']*\"[^']*'" tests/tests.js | head -3)"`, which has no line-start anchor. ship.sh:640 (vanished-tests gate) anchors with `^  test('`.

findings.problem: The reap pattern is a fixed list of binary names (Mac: 'Google Chrome'; Linux: chrome|chromium|chromium-browser) and is not derived from the binary fm_chrome / chrome_path actually picked. FM_CHROME is explicitly supported. If it points at a binary outside the list (Linux chrome-headless-shell or a renamed Chrome-for-Testing binary, Mac Chromium.app), pgrep matches 0 processes and ship.sh prints nothing. Orphans are never reaped, silently, which is the failure the port's own comment describes for the Mac pattern on Linux. The effect fails closed (orphans cause false reds or timeouts, not passes), hence minor.
findings.fix: Build the pattern from basename(fm_chrome), escaped, plus '.*fm-cdp-'. Alternatively, refuse (or at least warn) when FM_CHROME's basename is not covered by fm_chrome_reap_pattern.
findings.evidence: _platform.sh:155 `Linux)  echo '^([^ ]*/)?(chrome|chromium|chromium-browser)( |$).*fm-cdp-'`. ship.sh:133-137 prints only when `_ORPH -gt 0`. _platform.sh:134-135 accepts any executable FM_CHROME.

findings.where: tools/ship.sh:194, and the buster gate's sh() and the oldest-first gate's `except Exception: diff = ''` (ship.sh ~425-470)
findings.problem: The port fixed 'a failing git reads as nothing changed' in _srcfiles.py and _spottests.py, citing 'dubious ownership' and \\wsl.localhost as real Linux causes. ship.sh's own copies of the pattern were left alone. If `git diff --name-only HEAD` fails, _JSFILES is empty and the JS-parse gate is skipped with no message. The buster and order gates likewise read a failed git as 'nothing changed'. Today the ship still refuses later, because `git add`/`git commit` fail the same way, so this is not a ship-through.
findings.fix: Run the git listing outside the pipeline and check its status, for example `_jsl="$(git diff --name-only HEAD)" || { echo '❌ git failed …'; exit 1; }`. In the Python gates, use subprocess.run with a returncode check instead of swallowing the error.
findings.evidence: ship.sh:194 `_JSFILES="$( { git diff --name-only HEAD; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard; } | grep -E … | sort -u )"`, whose status is never checked. _srcfiles.py:14-22 now exits 2 on a git failure, for the reason stated in its own comment.

findings.where: tools/ship.sh:828 (no branch gate) vs tools/rollback.sh:97-102 and tools/inbox.sh:22-30
findings.problem: The port added a 'publishes main, so runs on main' gate to rollback.sh and inbox.sh, for exactly this hazard, but not to ship.sh, which always runs `git push -q ssh main`. Run from a non-main branch (a Mac work branch, which inbox.sh's comment says happens, or port/wsl once FM_SHIP_ALLOW_NON_MAC=1), ship.sh commits on that branch after ~90 minutes of suites. It then pushes whatever local main holds, including any unpushed main commits, and ends with 'PUSH DID NOT LAND'. This already happened before the port on the Mac, but the new switch-over flag makes it reachable on WSL.
findings.fix: Add the same `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` = main check near ship.sh's top (after the trap, with _WHY set), or push `HEAD:main` only when on main.
findings.evidence: rollback.sh:97 `_BRANCH="$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"; if [ "$_BRANCH" != main ]; then … exit 1`. ship.sh:828 `git push -q ssh main 2>&1 | tail -2` has no branch check anywhere in the file.

findings.where: tests/_cdp.py (launch flags; mouse gate at ~319-341 and ~476; reaper/profile sweep at ~251-287)
findings.problem: These are Mac behaviour changes in the runner every gate depends on, and the diff gives no sign they were run on the Mac. `--mute-audio` is now passed on the Mac too; the comment says 'measured', but the measurement describes WSLg. A new DID-NOT-RUN 'NO MOUSE' gate re-checks the top document's (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) after every real-input batch on the Mac too. The reaper pattern narrowed from 'fm-cdp-' to 'Google Chrome.*fm-cdp-'. Every $TMPDIR/fm-cdp-* folder is now deleted at start-up. Each is intended, but any of them could turn a Mac pass into DID NOT RUN or red (memory notes voice tests already depend on coreaudiod).
findings.fix: Before merging to main, run one full Mac pass at 1280 and one at 380, plus a `?only=921` slice and a real-touch test (queue 924), against dbd3bed2. Gate --mute-audio to Linux if anything audio-related moves.
findings.evidence: git diff b46b47d3 dbd3bed2 -- tests/_cdp.py: `+ "--mute-audio",` is unconditional. The `mouse.update(check=True …)` re-check runs regardless of OS. `_pat = _platform.reap_pattern()` returns 'Google Chrome.*fm-cdp-' on darwin. `glob(…/fm-cdp-*)` is followed by rmtree.

findings.problem: On WSL the load gate measures only the VM's /proc/loadavg. The usual WSL stall causes it names itself (Defender, the Search indexer, Vmmem short of memory) are invisible to it, and the bar of 1.6x the cores is unmeasured there. When it PASSES on WSL nothing says it could not see the host; the explanation appears only in a refusal. No free-memory gate exists on either OS: fm_swap_summary only feeds the message text. Dormant while the non-Mac ship gate holds.
findings.fix: When fm_is_wsl, print one line on pass, e.g. '⚠️ load gate sees the WSL VM only — Windows-side load is not measured'. Before the switch-over, consider a MemAvailable floor from /proc/meminfo.
findings.evidence: _platform.sh:47 comment '(Under WSL it is the VM's load; the Windows host's is not in it.)'; :58-59 'UNMEASURED on WSL's vCPUs'. ship.sh:165 is the only decision point and prints nothing on pass.

gates.summary:
I read tools/_platform.sh in full and every changed hunk in ship, prove, mutate, spotcheck, tick, inbox, _testfloor, rollback and next. I also read the helpers they call (_srcfiles.py, _spottests.py, tests/_platform.py, the _cdp.py exit paths, test-rollback.sh). Everything was read-only via git show and git diff; tests.js was not grepped, as the brief asked.

(a) Silent gates on Linux: I found no gate that now passes because a tool or value is missing.
- The load gate refuses when it cannot read the load (fm_ncpu, fm_load1 and fm_load_bar all return non-zero; there is no `|| echo 4`).
- The JS parse gate refuses when there is no parser, and node uses the same `new Function` check as jsc.
- A missing Chrome refuses, mutate.sh refuses on an empty hash, and a missing cmp or python3 refuses.
- mutate.sh's run that never finished now reads DID NOT RUN instead of SURVIVED.
- prove.sh and spotcheck.sh refuse when git or rsync fails, and a missing `expect` counts as a failure in test-rollback.sh.
- The NUL, ?v= buster and oldest-first gates are Python and behave the same on both machines.
- There is no free-memory gate; swap figures only appear in a message.
- The real gap is inbox.sh off main (major). It reads only ssh/main's INBOX.md and ignores the working tree, where the logging chat appends. On the WSL port branch, or a Mac work branch, tick.sh therefore shows 'inbox empty' plus an empty queue, because tick's sed also hides next.sh's STOP banner.
- Smaller gaps: the reap pattern does not follow FM_CHROME and silently matches nothing; ship.sh still reads a failing git as 'no JS changed' (the ship still fails later at commit); the WSL load gate is blind to Windows-side load and says nothing when it passes.

(b) Mac behaviour: the ship path is intact on Darwin.
- Same sysctl fields and bar (1.6x the cores), same jsc command and same suite_timeout maths.
- Unchanged: the .last-ship format, 'pushed and verified', `_whyslow` text and `pgrep -fl` (BSD) for tick.
- Changed on the Mac:
  - The double-quote-title regex is stricter and unanchored. Confirm it matches nothing in tests.js, or every Mac ship refuses.
  - spotcheck now gives no verdict, and blames the machine, when the control run does not finish. Before, that release was logged as `NOT-PROVEN NO-CONTROL`.
  - The mutate cap went from 1800 s to at least 3600 s, with a new exit 8.
  - inbox.sh now reads the Shortcuts folder even without FreeMotion-requests.txt and prints a new banner.
  - rollback.sh refuses off main.
  - _cdp.py adds --mute-audio, a mouse DID-NOT-RUN check, a narrower reaper and a profile sweep on the Mac too. Run one full Mac pass at each width before merging.
- ship.sh still has no main-branch check of its own.

(c) No quoting, set -e or pipefail mistake I found turns a failure into success.
- `var="$(cmd)" || refuse` is used correctly throughout.
- spotcheck's here-string loops run in the current shell, so their exits stop the script.
- The `&&`-list patterns in inbox.sh are unchanged from before.
- _platform.sh's top level is only exports and function definitions, so it is safe under `set -e` and `set -u`.

findings.problem: On Linux, real touch is sent without touch emulation, so for the whole gesture the page still reports a mouse: (hover: hover), (pointer: fine), maxTouchPoints 0. The comment says the only remaining difference is in js/collab-presence.js and js/collab-ui.js, and that is wrong. Touch-only CSS and fine-pointer JS run during a finger gesture on the Mac but take the mouse path on Linux. The driver gives the page no signal either: it only answers __fmInputErr and __fmInputDone. Real-touch tests exist because synthetic events missed his phone bugs, and on Linux they now run touch events against the mouse layout without saying so. A touch-layout regression can come back green on Linux and red on the Mac or phone, and prove.sh can mark a touch fix DEAD instead of CAUGHT.
findings.fix: Make the difference visible to the tests rather than describing it in a comment. Write the input mode into the app frame with every answer (e.g. w.__fmInputTouchEmulated = REAL_TOUCH_VIA_EMULATION). Have the real-input helper in tests.js fail by name when a test that depends on the finger's media state runs without it (an option like {needsTouchMedia:true}). Correct the comment in _platform.py to list the CSS and JS readers. Until then, treat a Linux green on any real-touch test as unproven.
findings.evidence: git grep at dbd3bed2 finds code that reads the pointer state outside the collab files. JS: js/app.js:1689 (frame-cache budget), js/elements-browser.js:171 (autofocus), js/home.js:3176 (hasKeyboard autofocus on the new-project dialog), js/settings.js:1116 (pointer: fine). CSS: styles.css:7762 (@media (hover: none): 44px .vr-* targets), styles.css:11480 (@media …,(hover: none),(pointer: coarse): 48px .pb-grip), plus 1129 and 10325. _platform.py:123-124 itself says the Mac shows 5 touch points and coarse during a gesture while Linux shows 0 and fine. The commit's WSL check ran only ?only=991/976 and ?only=export, none of them real-touch suites.

findings.where: tests/_cdp.py:256-263 and tools/ship.sh:124 (reaper liveness check); tests/_cdp.py:267-286
findings.problem: The reaper decides whether another run is in flight with `pgrep -f _cdp.py`. That matches ANY process whose command line contains the string, not just a running driver: a shell that is still running `python3 tests/_cdp.py …` (e.g. the Bash tool's wrapper shell), `timeout … python3 tests/_cdp.py`, or a ship.sh whose commit-message argument names _cdp.py (this commit's own message does). When that happens the reaper stands down without printing anything. The kill and the new fm-cdp-* profile cleanup are then skipped on exactly the runs most likely to leave orphans. The port fixed this same self-match in the kill pattern and in tick.sh (fm_pgrep_args) but not here. Two related gaps: (1) the reap pattern is fixed per OS, not taken from the Chrome actually launched. An FM_CHROME of chrome-headless-shell on Linux or Chromium.app on the Mac is never matched, so its orphans are never reaped, again silently (the only message is for 'no pattern for this OS'). (2) Probe Chromes on other profile prefixes (fm-shot-, fm-sweep-, fm-699-, …) are never reaped by anything.
findings.fix: Anchor the liveness pattern to the interpreter, e.g. '^[^ ]*python[0-9.]* ([^ ]+ )*[^ ]*tests/_cdp\.py( |$)', in both _cdp.py and ship.sh. When standing down, print the matching PIDs and command lines to stderr. Check that the resolved Chrome's basename is covered by the reap pattern and say so on stderr when it is not, or build the pattern from the resolved binary.
findings.evidence: _cdp.py:257: subprocess.run(["pgrep", "-f", "_cdp.py"]); only os.getpid() is excluded, not parent shells. ship.sh:124: elif ! pgrep -f '_cdp\.py'. In both, the in-flight skip prints nothing; only the pgrep-missing case (_cdp.py:259-261) and the no-pattern case (267-270) print. The commit message of dbd3bed2 contains 'tests/_cdp.py:' and tools/ship.sh takes the message as argv. Reap pattern: _platform.py:113 and _platform.sh:155. The wrapper-shell case is plausible from how the Bash tool spawns commands; not measured here.

findings.problem: If google-chrome is missing, Chromium on PATH is used without any notice. Neither the driver's JSON nor ship.sh's preflight (`fm_chrome >/dev/null`) ever records which browser or version ran. chrome_path's own docstring calls running a different browser 'a silent substitution' and refuses it for a wrong FM_CHROME, but allows it for the PATH fallback. Chromium builds can differ in exactly what the app probes at runtime: the H.264 encoder candidates (exporter.js:974-977) and AAC encoding (exporter.js:878, 1091, 1293). A test that returns early when a codec is unsupported then passes untested, which is the same shape as the 976 rail early-returns the port gated against. Ubuntu's chromium-browser is a snap with a private /tmp, so its real profile lands outside the folder _cdp.py deletes.
findings.fix: Put the browser in every result: call Browser.getVersion over CDP and add "browser": "<path> <product>" to every _cdp.py JSON, including did-not-run results, and print it on ship.sh's suite line. Accept chromium/chromium-browser only when FM_CHROME names one explicitly; otherwise refuse with the install hint.
findings.evidence: PATH_NAMES = ("google-chrome", "google-chrome-stable", "chromium", "chromium-browser") at _platform.py:19; for loop 40-43 returns the first hit. ship.sh:231 discards fm_chrome's stdout. The commit records 9 export reds on Linux Chrome itself ('environment, not the port'), so codec-dependent paths already differ between machines.

findings.problem: _shot.sh launches Linux Chrome without the flags _platform.py says Linux needs to answer like the Mac (the --blink-settings mouse), and without TMPDIR in the profile. On Linux, every _shot.sh picture is drawn as (hover: none)/(pointer: none): the finger layout, even at PC widths. Nothing says so. tools/shot.py got a gate for exactly this (shot.py:98-101) but its sister tool did not, and these are pictures Ezra picks designs from. Each launch also leaves the /tmp/com.google.Chrome.* entries that chrome_env exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Add fm_chrome_extra_flags to tools/_platform.sh as the twin of chrome_extra_flags(), with the same text, and pass it plus TMPDIR to Chrome in _shot.sh. Or have _shot.sh refuse at PC widths on Linux and point to tools/shot.py.
findings.evidence: The launch line is `"$CHROME" --headless --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --mute-audio --force-device-scale-factor=2 …`, with no --blink-settings and no env. _platform.py:79-85 says Linux headless has hover:none, pointer:none without the blink settings.

findings.problem: `import websocket` is unguarded. On a fresh Ubuntu 24.04, where system-wide pip install is blocked (PEP 668), the driver's very first run dies with a ModuleNotFoundError traceback and exit 1. The docstring (line 23) now promises exit 1 means 'red'. ship.sh then prints 'THE SUITE DID NOT RUN' with no reason, because it only greps the JSON "error" field (ship.sh:775, 810), and the traceback is swallowed into $OUT. It is loud but cannot be diagnosed. Uncaught raises at 304-306 (Page.enable / Runtime.enable / Page.navigate) and 550 (json.loads) also still exit 1 as tracebacks. Consumers parse the JSON, so this is safe, but the '1 = red' contract is not true.
findings.fix: Wrap the import: on ImportError print _did_not_run("websocket-client is not installed — sudo apt install python3-websocket") and exit 2. Also preflight it in ship.sh next to fm_chrome. Either wrap main's body so any uncaught exception becomes a did-not-run result, or fix the docstring.
findings.evidence: _cdp.py:29 `import websocket  # websocket-client` sits at module top, before _did_not_run exists. No tool under tools/ checks for the module (git grep 'websocket' in tools/*.sh finds nothing).

findings.problem: The new mouse gate has two gaps. (a) It evaluates run.html's own `matchMedia`, which page script can replace. A stub on the top window would answer for a page that has lost its mouse. (b) The driver writes __fmInputDone right after re-arming the check (480), so the next tests start before the mouse has been re-verified. The gate needs 4 False answers in a row (~1 s), and a run whose payload arrives inside that window reports its verdict anyway. Neither can happen on Linux today, because emulation is never toggled there. As the backstop for 'every mouse-gated test would pass or fail for the wrong reason', though, it can be bypassed.
findings.fix: Before writing __fmInputDone, confirm the mouse is back, polling until it is or ending as did-not-run; the test then cannot continue on a mouseless page. Evaluate MOUSE_QUERY in an isolated world (Page.createIsolatedWorld, then Runtime.evaluate with that contextId) so no test stub can answer for the browser.
findings.evidence: _mouse_state: cdp.eval("matchMedia(%s).matches" …) runs in the page's main world. mouse.update(check=True…) at 478 is followed immediately by the __fmInputDone write at 479-480; the gate itself only runs at the top of the next loop iteration (331).

findings.problem: --mute-audio is added to the Mac's command line too. That contradicts the port's own rule in gl_flags, 'The Mac keeps the flags its known-good runs were measured with' (_platform.py:67). The only measurement quoted ('the AudioContext still runs, at 44100') was taken in WSL. The commit asks the PM to check Mac-affecting changes but does not list this one. A muted WebContents can route output to a muted or fake sink with different timing, and the Mac's voice:/audio tests already have a coreaudiod-sensitive history.
findings.fix: Make --mute-audio Linux-only like the GL flags, or record one green Mac full pass at both widths with it before merging.
findings.evidence: _cdp.py:85 adds "--mute-audio" unconditionally, and _kbdevice.py:368 does the same. The commit's 'ALSO FIXED (affect the Mac too — please check)' list does not include it.

findings.problem: The port checks the mouse (and overlay scrollbars), but not fonts. The app's font stack starts with Apple fonts (-apple-system, SF Pro Display), which Linux does not have, so it falls back to Inter or a generic sans. Every text-width, wrap and clipping measurement at 380px, and every text-bearing pixel hash, is taken in a font that is on neither his iPhone nor the Mac. A label-clipping regression like queue 431 can pass on Linux if the fallback is narrower. Nothing records which font was used.
findings.fix: Add a startup fidelity check next to the mouse gate. Measure a reference string's width in the app's resolved font and compare it with a recorded Mac value: warn when it differs, or refuse when it differs a lot. Or install a metric-compatible font and pin it with fontconfig.
findings.evidence: styles.css:121 `font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Display", "Segoe UI", Inter, sans-serif;`. git grep -i font in tests/_platform.py, tools/_platform.sh and tests/_cdp.py finds nothing.

driver.summary:
The Linux test driver is careful, and none of the new code turns a red run into "ok": true. Exit codes, ship.sh's '"ok": true' check, mutate.sh's suite_ran and _spotjudge are intact. Every new did-not-run path exits 2 with FAIL rewritten to 'fail', so a run that never happened cannot read as green or as CAUGHT.

What holds up:
- **Missing Chrome:** handled loudly everywhere it is looked up — _cdp.py (exit 2, before any profile is made), ship.sh preflight, _kbdevice, shot.py, _shot.sh. A wrong FM_CHROME refuses instead of falling back.
- **Flags:** --mute-audio, --disable-features=WebRtcHideLocalIpsWithMdns and --allow-loopback-in-peer-connection are on every _cdp.launch. The Linux GL choice (--disable-gpu --enable-unsafe-swiftshader) is reasoned and measured.
- **Sandbox:** there is no --no-sandbox anywhere, so a root run fails with Chrome's own message captured.
- **Clean-up:** profiles are deleted on every exit path, with a retry on Linux. Leftover fm-cdp-* folders are swept at startup.
- **Reap pattern:** the Linux pattern is identical in the .py and .sh files, anchored to the Chrome binary, and needs fm-cdp- in the command line. It cannot kill the user's own Chrome.
- **Network:** the DevTools port and serve.sh are on 127.0.0.1. Chrome resolves *.localhost to loopback by itself, and nothing in the port touches the tier-3 frame loading. The commit's WSL verification never ran ?only=921, though.

The one major gap is real touch on Linux. It is sent without emulation, so during a gesture the page keeps (hover: hover)/(pointer: fine). Touch-only CSS and fine-pointer JS take the mouse path, and _platform.py's claim that only the collab files notice is wrong. Touch-layout regressions can be green on Linux and red on the phone, and tests get no signal that this happened.

Smaller items:
- The reaper's `pgrep -f _cdp.py` check also matches wrapper shells and commit messages, and then stands down silently. The reap pattern is not derived from FM_CHROME.
- Chromium is accepted silently, and no result records which browser ran.
- _shot.sh lacks the Linux mouse flags, so its PC shots on Linux are the finger layout.
- `import websocket` is unguarded: on a fresh Ubuntu the first run dies with a traceback, and ship.sh shows no reason.
- The mouse gate can be fooled by a page-script stub and lets tests proceed before it re-verifies.
- --mute-audio changes the Mac's command line without a Mac measurement.
- There is no font-parity check.

Fix the touch signal before using Linux runs as proof of touch behaviour. The rest are cheap structural hardening.
